Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when high blood pressure may be present, but they do not provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they require regular calibration with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to offer full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, citing clinical trial results involving thousands of participants…

The silent killer

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) both pose serious health threats.

Of the two, high blood pressure is more dangerous and is known as the "silent killer" — it can cause serious and irreversible damage to the arteries, heart and brain without obvious symptoms. Many people only discover they have the problem after a heart attack or stroke.

For older people, regular blood pressure measurement is ideal. There are many easy-to-use upper-arm blood pressure monitors available for home use. However, a fitness device that can be worn all day and monitor automatically would be even more ideal.

Apple Watch blood pressure feature

With the release of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can now measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models do not provide any readings — they only issue alerts when possible signs of high blood pressure are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but require periodic calibration using readings from an upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup Vital Signals says its Signal Ring smart ring requires no calibration, yet offers accuracy comparable to traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitors.

CEO Tom Moss told Bloomberg that he nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure — an experience that drove him to found the company.

The Signal Ring opens for pre-order later today, ships in October, and is priced at US$399 with no subscription required. The companion mobile app can display real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trends (as shown above).

Worth noting: the Oura Ring has not yet received approval from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), though clinical trials show it can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss is not particularly keen on marketing the Signal Ring to all consumers. He says the feature is best suited for older people, and those assessed by doctors as being at risk of high blood pressure — a comment that suggests the Signal Ring may be unremarkable in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
